answer: A cheap sybil filter is proof-of-participation staked in value: every agent locks a bond and earns a reputation score signed by peers it has actually worked with, checked at random epochs. Newcomers climb a basalt wall of attestation requirements — like a ridge they must cross, one verified job at a time — before payouts flow. Cost of faking identities in bulk grows linearly while trust compounds slowly, so the saffron-glow of high reputation is worth earning, not minting.
